question.leadin: Answer the following about the Edo period.
question.text: This is the modern-day name of the city of Edo, for which the Edo period was named. It is also the modern-day capital of Japan.
question.clue: The Place That Was Promised and Underground chronicled a terrorist attack in this city carried out by a group now called Aleph.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about emperors of Japan.
swap.text: This emperor modernized Japan during the 19th century under his namesake "restoration." This man was presented with the Charter Oath, the first constitution of modern Japan.
swap.answerHtml: Emperor Meiji [may-ee-jee] (accept Meiji the Great or Mutsuhito ) – Page 4 – Packet 8
swap.clue: This man's governing philosophy was outlined in thefive point "Charter Oath" and would lead to the creation of the position of Prime Minister along with a largely powerless parliament.

question.leadin: Give the following about earthquakes that have devastated Japan.
question.text: Both the 2011 and 1923 earthquakes were centered near this largest Japanese island.
question.clue: By far the largest of the four main islands is this one, home to Tokyo, Kyoto, and Nagoya.

swap.leadin: This work depicts three fishing boats swept up in the title object near present-day Yokohama. --.
swap.text: Name this Hokusai print depicting Mount Fuji in the background.
swap.answerHtml: The <u>Great Wave off Kanagawa</u> (or <u>Kanagawa-oki</u> <u>nami</u> <u>ura</u>; or <u>Under the Wave off Kanagawa</u>)
swap.clue: This woodblock print by Hokusai that depicts three fishing boats caught in the title phenomenon near the title location while traveling back towards Edo.

question.leadin: This battle saw the use of Portuguese arquebuses, and one side of this battle consisted of forces loyal to Toyotomi Hideyori.
question.text: Name this battle that saw the forces of Ishida Mitsunari and Mori Terumoto defeated by those of Tokugawa Ieyasu, thereby establishing his namesake shogunate.
question.clue: The capture of Konosu and Gifu Castles preceded this battle, whose decisive moment saw a staged round of arquebus fire signal a force of turncoats to attack the army of their initial ally Otani instead.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the usage of planes during World War II.
swap.text: The Mitsubishi Zero which was developed in this country possessed a notoriously thin aluminum skin which allowed it to be agile at the cost of protection. This country encouraged kamikaze pilots three years after it bombed Pearl Harbor.
swap.clue: The Stimson Doctrine was adopted to counter the ambitions of this country.

question.leadin: This city is the largest in the Chugoku region of Honshu, but it is unfortunately not known for its museums, schools, or other attractions.
question.text: Name this Japanese city best known for being atom-bombed, along with Nagasaki. The bomb dropped on this city was from an aircraft named for a pilot's mother, the Enola Gay.
question.clue: A bell with the phrase "know yourself" commemorates an incident in this city that created the first hibakusha ("HEE-ba-KOO-sha").

swap.text: The Ashikaga Shogunate was based in this city of Japan, which was known as Heian during an earlier period. It's not Tokyo, but the english translation for this city is "capital city."
swap.clue: The historic shrines and religious landmarks of this city survive today because Henry Stimson prevented it from being targeted with the atomic bomb.

question.text: He set into motion the Kemmu Restoration, which overthrew Kamakura rule. For 15 points, name this Japanese emperor whose 1333 destruction of the first shogunate only cleared the way for Ashikaga Takauji to displace him and form a new line of shoguns.
question.clue: He escaped from the Oki Islands to take advantage of the suicide of an opponent who spent his days watching dog fights, but he ultimately broke with his supporters by naming Morinaga as regent, leading to Kogon pressing a rival claim to the throne.

swap.leadin: Moderator note: do not reveal the alternate answer to the first bonus part. The man who negotiated this treaty gave the emperor an ultimatum from President Fillmore and then left the country for a year.
swap.text: Identify this 1854 treaty which opened up the ports of Shimoda and Hakodate in Japan to American trade.
swap.clue: Signed aboard the USS Powhatan, one provision of it mandated hospitality to shipwrecked sailors and their free travel within certain limits.

question.leadin: Name the following people involved in the opening of Japanese ports to American trade.
question.text: This man sailed into Uraga Harbor near Edo in 1852 and refused to leave until the Tokugawa Shogunate received a letter he had brought from the President.
question.clue: This American Commodore enforced the signing of the Kanagawa Treaty and helped to open Japan's doors by leading his fleet the "Black Ships."

swap.leadin: This man's favorite pastime was falconry.
swap.text: Name this victor at the Battle of Sekigahara, who signed the Christian Expulsion Edict in 1614. His forces successfully besieged Osaka to kill Toyotomi Hideyori.
swap.answerHtml: Tokugawa Ieyasu [or Matsudaira Takechiyo, either part, or Motonobu or Motoyasu]
swap.clue: As head of the Eastern Army, this man defeated the forces of Ishida Mitsunari at the Battle of Sekigahara.

question.leadin: The Zenkunen war was fought during the end of this period, which also saw the flourishing of poetry and the arts.
question.text: Name this period of Japanese history that begin after Emperor Kammu moved the capital from Nara to modern-day Kyoto in the late 700s.
question.clue: Starting in this period, proprietors called ryoke would hand money to government inspectors to preserve the tax-free status of their sh¯oen estates.

swap.leadin: The Inariyama Sword, which contains Japanese written in Chinese characters, was dated to this period of Japanese history.
swap.text: Name this part of the Yamato period which transitioned to the Asuka period with the introduction of Buddhism to Japan. This Japanese era was named after large keyhole-shaped tombs.
swap.clue: This period of Japanese history following the Yayoi period is named after giant keyhole-shaped burial mounds.

question.text: Landscapes and portraiture became more common in scroll art, and the predominant school of ikebana arose, during this period of Japanese history from 1337 to 1573.
question.clue: This shogunate that followed the Kenmu Restoration.

swap.leadin: This text, whose name is sometimes translated as "Chronicles of Japan," is the second-oldest extant piece of Japanese literature after the Kojiki.
swap.text: Name this set of chronicles, the most comprehensive text available for scholarship on Ancient Japan. It was completed under the supervision of Prince Toneri and presented to Empress Gensho in the year 720.
swap.clue: This historical work claims that Emperor Tenmu played sugoroku, a backgammon-like game that was later banned due to its players' propensity for gambling. Unlike the Kojiki, this work of history extends until the 8th century.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Jomon and Epi-Jomon cultures and peoples.
question.text: The term "Zoku" or "Epi-" Jomon refers to the persistence of Jomon patterns in northern Japan past when this culture superseded it further south. Wet rice agriculture became dominant in this culture's namesake period.

swap.leadin: Identify these leaders of 20th century Japan.
swap.text: This man served as Emperor of Japan from 1912 to 1926. His reign is considered a golden age of Japanese democracy.
swap.clue: This ruler, who ceded regency power to his son due to psychological problems. His country sent a list of twenty-one demands to a neighbor.

question.text: The Russo-Japanese war was partly precipitated by this 1895 action, in which Russia, France, and Germany forced Japan to return the Liaodong Peninsula to China.

swap.text: The Tokugawa shogun Iemitsu instituted this system, which required each of the daimyo to spend a part of the year in Edo and leave family members as hostages in order to prevent rebellion.
